correctness.rationale: For all \(0<a<1\) the domain is a square minus exactly four right triangles. The triangular cosine integral gives the complete integer Fourier formula, with a separately verified diagonal limit. Cosine and sine zero identities give necessary-and-sufficient rational congruences. Exact inclusion–exclusion produces all finite-cutoff zero counts and limiting frequencies. Four triangular overlaps, no triple overlaps, give three atom probabilities; torus Parseval gives the sum of squared Fourier coefficients. Both proof and 252 integer-count, 20,519 Fourier, 12 quadrature, four coverage, two partial-Parseval checks reconstructed.

value.rationale: The natural integer Fourier support of a continuously varying convex octagon jumps sharply in arithmetic structure: irrational cut has no zero at nonzero integer frequencies; reduced rational cut supports explicit congruence lines with exact finite and asymptotic densities. This determines all pairwise integer exponential orthogonality. The same polygon family has a geometric sharp double-coverage onset and an exact Fourier energy sum with a derivative singularity. Such exact dual arithmetic/overlap information is germane to spectrality and lattice covering rather than a routine unmotivated finite slice.
